name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with incumbent Scott Peters running
Peters holds $2.6M cash vs. no reported fundraising for Cohen
No public polling of the general
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Peters: a D+10 district, incumbency, and a large cash advantage over a challenger with no reported fundraising. Markets price him around 95%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race, or significant outside spending against Peters, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He advanced to the general election and enters with roughly $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Steve Cohen has no reported fundraising or cash reserves. No outside groups are spending against Peters, and no public polls of the race are available.
Prediction markets put Peters' chances near 95 percent, and the fundamentals point the same way: the district lean, incumbency, and a large money edge all favor the incumbent. With no polling and no expert ratings to refine the picture, uncertainty stays somewhat elevated, but every available signal points to Peters winning comfortably.
